checks.why: a one-parameter lambda converts only to the one-parameter delegate overload
a two-parameter lambda converts only to the two-parameter delegate overload
a string literal converts to neither a delegate nor a class in source with no conversion: the string overload
a lambda converts to no predefined type
a source-typed argument converts only to what its type implements
the interface it does not implement is not a candidate
a string argument does not convert to an exception: the template overload
the exception overload is not called with a string in that position
control: two delegates of the same parameter count are not told apart by a lambda's shape: the call stays one of the set
an interface-typed argument converts to no class in source
the class overload is not called with an interface value
a lambda converts to no class in source
explicit type arguments pick the generic overload
the non-generic overload is not called with type arguments
